identity_code.definition: A system of recurring elements that enables a person, organization, or institution to remain recognizable even when its name is absent.

v1.name: Kelly Code V1
v1.title: The Theory of Recognizability
v1.limitation: Recognizability alone does not explain long-term identity survival.

v2.name: Kelly Code V2
v2.title: The Theory of Portability
v2.core_thesis: The true value of identity is measured not by its creation, but by its transferability.
v2.definition: Portability is the ability of an Identity Code to preserve recognizability and meaning across environmental transitions.

levels.name: Platform Transition
levels.definition: Identity moves into a new medium.

levels.name: Role Transition
levels.definition: Identity acquires a new social role.

v2.law_of_portability: The more different environments in which the same Identity Code remains recognizable, the stronger the identity.

conclusion.statement: The Kelly Code is a theory of identity survival.
conclusion.final_principle: Identity becomes historically significant when its code survives its original context.
